stage: All five unmarked full images and all seven wider raw crops inspected; observations saved before label overlays.
scope: Seven known historical exclusions across five images; region selection is historical-label informed. Reviewer has prior case knowledge and is not an independently blinded human. No prediction overlays are used for decisions.

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: stacked white cassette fronts occupy the metal rack; a white handheld gripper and hand occlude the central lower area. A small white surface is visible between the jaws below the rack. Surface ownership there requires a wider local view; no point assigned from the full photo.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: A narrow white sliver lies immediately to the right of the bottom rack divider and to the left of the thumb, separate from the broad front in the leftmost column. Most of the adjacent cassette is covered by the thumb.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: The lower sliver is plausibly the frontal remainder of the neighboring cassette; its upper continuation includes receding surface material, so a long strip must not automatically be boxed as all front. The metal divider separates it from the already visible left-column cassette.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: The lower tip is soft and close to the thumb/rack boundaries. A possible lower-left turn exists, but a precise independently observed corner cannot yet be asserted from this crop. The other corner is covered.
uncertainties: Tight upper extent of the remaining frontal material
Whether the tiny lower turn is independently locatable rather than an occluder junction

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: similar rack and gripper arrangement, with the foreground gripper covering lower central cassette material. A narrow white surface remains visible between the jaws; determining front versus tool or cassette top requires local inspection.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: A narrow white sliver remains on the rack side of the thumb, to the right of the lowest left-column front and its separating upright.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: The region follows a cassette-like white surface behind the thumb. The lower small frontal remnant should be separated from the longer receding upper-surface strip; the broad neighboring front is a different object.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: The far corner is hidden by the thumb. The small bottom tip may be a left lower turn, but its exact localization is softened and potentially mixed with the thumb boundary.
uncertainties: Tight upper extent of frontal versus receding material
Reliability of the small lower-left turn

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: tilted rack with cassette stacks near the top frame and in two lower columns; the uppermost right-column white material meets the image boundary. The empty foreground gripper is separate from the rack. Top clipped fronts require distinction from the molded upper rim of the next visible front.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: At the upper image edge of the rightmost stack, a small white wedge remains above the next broad front. A slanted lower contour and narrow darker separation are visible, supporting a distinct clipped front rather than a second row for the broad front.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: The repeated front contours establish distinct visible bands; the tiny upper wedge is contiguous cassette material and is bounded by the image edge, not rack.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: A left-side lower turn appears inside the image near the upper-left of the column. Its right counterpart would extend above the frame and must not be invented at the image border.
uncertainties: Nominal lower-left coordinate has several-pixel softness
Exact top-edge intersection of the slanted lower contour

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: rack front is filled by multiple stacks; gripper obscures central lower material. The bottom-left rack column reaches the bottom image boundary, where a slanted white surface is clipped. Need local contour inspection to distinguish neighboring fronts rather than infer from spacing.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: The lowest left rack column reaches the bottom frame. A thin lower white band is visible beneath the lower turn of the broader front immediately above it.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: There is a lower contour break between the broad upper face and the small lower band. This supports a separate bottom-clipped front, while the overlapping axis-aligned envelopes alone would not establish duplication.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: The lower band continues outside the frame before either actual lower corner can be confidently located. The frame edge is not a substitute lower edge or landmark.
uncertainties: The narrow band transition is blurred; its top and left extrema need nominal visual adjudication
The nearby broad face and hand create possible competing boundary cues

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: several lower central bands are visible to the left of the gripper. Small white pieces also occur between and beside the jaws. Some are rim or top surfaces; physical ownership must be judged independently of repetition. The former row 52 region was encountered in earlier R65 work and is not a blinded new region.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: The lowest of the visible stacked bands immediately to the left of the gripper is a separate short cassette front. A narrow dark separation distinguishes it from the band above.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: White frontal material runs from the stack left edge to the gripper occlusion; it is neither the rack upright nor gripper material.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: The left lower turn is visible. The right part is covered by the gripper, so the gripper boundary cannot supply a right corner.

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: several lower central bands are visible to the left of the gripper. Small white pieces also occur between and beside the jaws. Some are rim or top surfaces; physical ownership must be judged independently of repetition. The former row 52 region was encountered in earlier R65 work and is not a blinded new region.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: A short white fragment appears between the right edge of the gripper jaw and the right rack border near the rack bottom.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: It is behind the gripper and continuous with the cassette surface in the last rack column. The visible lower band ends against dark rack below, supporting a cassette front distinct from the gripper.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: The right lower turn appears visible near the rack boundary; the left part is covered by the jaw.
uncertainties: Soft right lower contour and nominal coordinate
Upper limit of frontal material versus the receding top surface

cases.raw_full_image_observation: Full unmarked image: several lower central bands are visible to the left of the gripper. Small white pieces also occur between and beside the jaws. Some are rim or top surfaces; physical ownership must be judged independently of repetition. The former row 52 region was encountered in earlier R65 work and is not a blinded new region.

raw_crop_observation.visible_instance: A small light frontal-looking strip remains in the gap between the jaws, below a larger angular light patch and a gray receding surface.
raw_crop_observation.ownership: A cassette-front interpretation is plausible from continuity behind the jaws, but the angular patch and narrow lower strip could be confused with part of the white gripper. Physical ownership of this central strip needs explicit adjudication; stack spacing alone is insufficient.
raw_crop_observation.corner_availability: Neither actual lower side junction is clearly visible. The jaw boundaries and small polygon corners are not established cassette lower corners.
uncertainties: Cassette versus gripper ownership of the central light strip
Whether the upper patch and lower strip belong to one physical front or to different surfaces
